title: session-bridger-playbook-scratch
content:
Context: quick personal sketch for a small feature bundle I'll prototype before next sprint. Goal is to enable cheap, robust handoff of a live conversation from hosted API to Dedicated/private runtimes (and across model variants) while preserving UX continuity and keeping token costs in check. This is rough — lots of questions marked TODO.

Problem statement
- Customers building assistants want to move an active session (chat) between environments or model classes without losing context or blowing up token costs.
- Typical flows: hosted -> dedicated (enterprise upgrade), dedicated -> private (air-gapped), fallback to smaller cheaper model when load spikes.
- Existing options: full convo replay (expensive), KV-store checkpointing (partial), session-level pointers (stateless but lossy). We need a middle ground.

High-level idea: "Session Bridger"
- Capture a compact, incremental representation of the conversation that can be serialized and rehydrated by a different runtime variant.
- Representation is layered:
  1) Structural metadata (participants, model pinned, encryption key id)
  2) Semantic checkpoints: small extracted summary + anchors (timestamped utterance ids)
  3) Minimal KV cache snapshot (only active recent keys or prefix tokens selected by heuristics)
  4) Optional deterministic compression blob (lossy quantized deltas for long-term context)
- Bridge format should be versioned and backward compatible (v0, v1 with anchors, v2 with token deltas).

User stories
- As a product admin, I can request an export bundle for a session so I can migrate to Dedicated without manual prompt engineering.
  Acceptance: export < 2s for sessions <= 10 turns, size < 8KB typical, includes model metadata and summary.
- As a client app, I can call /sessions/{id}/bridge?target=dedicated-xyz and receive a signed package that can be loaded into the target runtime to resume with minimal chattiness.
  Acceptance: resumed assistant continues coherent thread in 1-2 prompt rounds; token overhead <= 30% vs full replay.
- As an SRE, I can trigger automatic fallback to smaller model using a Bridge profile that reduces KV snapshot size and forces summary-first rehydrate.
  Acceptance: fallback occurs automatically under policy; user-visible latency change < 200ms; economic saving measured.

Technical notes / heuristics (brainstorm)
- Summarizer: lightweight extractive+abstractive pipeline that produces 160–400 char anchor summaries per topic change.
- Anchor selection: treat system messages and user clarifying questions as anchors; drop long assistant-only monologues unless referenced.
- KV snapshot policy: keep last N k-v entries where tokens predicted to be reused (heuristic: top-k token reuse frequency in last M tokens), otherwise only keep keys for in-flight tool calls.
- Compression: use byte-pair tokenized compression then LZ for cross-runtime portability. Consider best-effort lossy delta for really long sessions.
- Security: sign + optional envelope encryption using customer's KMS key id; bridges expire after TTL.

Edge cases / TODOs
- Multi-device: what if two clients try to resume simultaneously? Need optimistic locking + merge strategy.
- Tool state: external tool outputs (file ids, attachments) — include stable references or fetch-on-demand.
- Persona/temperature drift: include model config snapshot; decide whether to force re-eval of safety layers on resume.
- Regulatory: private deployments may disallow sending any raw user tokens off-host — need to support redact-first bridge.
- Latency/cost trade: how to auto-select between "full replay" (accurate) and "bridged resume" (cheap) based on SLOs.

Prototype plan (minimal viable experiment)
1) Simple Bridge v0: structural metadata + single 2-sentence summary + last 3 turns plaintext. Implement export/import hooks in hosted API only.
2) Measure: 50 sessions > 10 turns, compare resume coherence vs full replay (human eval A/B) and token delta. Collect failure cases.
3) If coherence delta < 10% and token savings > 40%, iterate v1 with KV snapshot and signature + basic encrypt.

Metrics to track
- Resume coherence score (human/auto eval) over A/B
- Token overhead vs full replay
- Export size distribution
- Resume latency (import time)
- Failure modes: incoherent resumes / missing tool references / security exceptions

UI/UX considerations (quick)
- Admin console: session > Export bridge (dropdown: target type, TTL, redact level)
- Client SDK: resume() method that accepts bridge blob and callback for missing references (fetch attachments)
- Error states surfaced to end user: graceful fallback message and retry button.

Risks
- Too lossy -> bad user experience (user sees wrong state)
- Cross-runtime incompatibilities (tokenizer differences, model config) -> guardrails needed
- Complexity of secure export for private deployments -> may increase support cost

Next steps (short)
- Pair with Mika to implement v0 export endpoint prototype (1 sprint)
- Set up small human eval harness (Ravi + UX researcher)
- Quick spike: measure tokenized size and resume round-trip time on local dev cluster

Notes to self
- Keep API footprint tiny; don't try to solve every edge immediately.
- Focus on visible wins for Dedicated onboarding and economic fallback policies.
- Document a simple fallback policy mapping (when to choose bridged resume vs replay).
__note: personal scratchpad — informal, iterative. Not for wide distribution until v1 vetted.
